chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever acquires wealth from that which is not permissible, Allah causes to be dominant over him the construction, and the water, and the clay.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical consequence of earning haram wealth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the concept of *gharar* (uncertainty) and divine retribution in economic transactions, where 'construction, water, and clay' symbolize the physical decay of the body or the stagnation of wealth, preventing its intended benefit. Scholars interpret this as a spiritual and physical consequence of consuming *haram* wealth, linking material accumulation to bodily deterioration or loss of barakah. This serves as a practical warning for believers to ensure the purity of their income sources to maintain both worldly stability and spiritual health.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who gathers wealth from other than Permissible means, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Cause him to be overcome by the construction, and the water, and the clay’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one earns an asset through unlawful means Allah overpowers him by means of building, water and clay.”’
